result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): The screenshots only show questions 1–2 and the start of question 3, so I can't see the remaining questions, the submit button, the results view or how a missing answer is handled. Scores for items 1, 2 and 5 are therefore partly inferred from what is visible. In that visible part, both quizzes are plain, sensible multiple-choice checks with no invented figures; each points users to the truck's data plate for load capacity. A uses a legible dark theme with clearly sized radio buttons, while B is a bright, high-contrast design whose radio buttons are slightly small and sit higher than their labels — a minor difference, so I rated them equal. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both screenshots show only the first two of five questions. Both pages use the same clean fieldset layout, and the content is plausible: each points to the truck's data plate for capacity instead of inventing figures, and each has a sensible pedestrian question. Neither screenshot shows the speed or parking questions, the submit button or the results state, so rubric items 1, 2 and 5 are only partly verifiable and I scored them the same for both. Nothing visible separates them beyond A's light theme versus B's dark theme.
